review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: It is argued that school need to rewarded students depend on their best academic results or their improvements. Personally, I strongly believe that academic rewards should be given to both regardless of their final outcome or their improvements.

On the one hand, it is reasonable to give presents to students who have outstanding in achievements. Given that students have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, are leading to propel towards overall academic gains. Furthermore, this kind of competition can be seen in almost every aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded. This also help student be used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition and enable them to achieve success in later life.

On the other hand, it is also beneficial to rewarding students who cut down significant improvements. Naturally, only a few students can come first and receive the rewards, causing others to think that their efforts futile because of not surpassing those outstanding individual. This makes students prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened. Consequently, they gradually lose the incentive to study. Moreover, emphasizing improvements could to encourage all students to be diligent in their studies, this also help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves who are irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. This can lead to have the constant desire to outdo themselves and benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that students who are outstanding in academic result or who show improvements should be rewarded, they can see it as recognization to their.
review.overall: Em trả lời đủ hai quan điểm và nhất quán với ý kiến thưởng cả học sinh có thành tích cao lẫn học sinh tiến bộ. Em triển khai được cả bốn chuỗi ý Cô giao, đặc biệt là nỗ lực → phần thưởng → động lực và chỉ thưởng số ít → nản chí → mất động lực. Em cần ưu tiên viết mỗi ý thành câu hoàn chỉnh có chủ ngữ, động từ chính và quan hệ rõ; khi câu đã đúng khung, các cụm tốt em dùng như “their praises and privileges”, “propel towards overall academic gains”, “thrive in the face of fierce competition” và “outdo themselves” sẽ phát huy rất rõ.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that dangerous sports should be prohibited by law, while other say that individuals must be free to take part in any activity. Personally, I am on the latter school of thought, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, It is justifiable to people say that these activities should be banned, given that even a minor error can lead directly to a death of participant, that can be seen in skydiving. However, a prohibition is impossible, because these sports are held [chưa đọc rõ] remote locations say, mountain cliff where surveillance is minimal. Add to that is the fact that the policy is unrealistic, it is unrealistic to expect a police officer follow every individual. Consequently, a prohibition exist only on paper and even worse that such policy drives practice underground, which are harder to ensure basic safety standards.

However, It is more logical that people are permitted to do any sports, as long as they understand risks and receive sufficient training. For example, in deep ocean diving where there are reputable club that offer participant appropriate equipment and qualified supervision, the teaching also makes the safety leading to better and safer experiences. This can be seen in the way newbie are accompanied by an expert who can taught them what to do when accidents occur that provides players an ability to recognise dangers and respond appropriately. Despite proper training giving people necessary practice that [chưa đọc rõ] participation safer, there are no activity with entirely risk-free.
In conclusion, banning is neither practical nor effective and I strongly convinced that people have freedom to choose, under strict conditions of training and awareness is a more realistic approach.

Tuy vậy, Body 1 lặp “the policy is unrealistic, it is unrealistic”, còn Body 2 ghép sai “the teaching also makes the safety leading” và “who can taught”. Đó là lỗi dựng câu cơ bản lặp ở những mắt xích quan trọng; bài còn cẩu thả ở khâu dựng câu và tự soát. Cô giữ những chữ bị ghi đè chưa đọc chắc ngoài phạm vi bắt lỗi. paragraphs: There is an opinion that dangerous sports should be prohibited by law, while others argue that individuals should be free to take part in any activity. Personally, I am of the latter school of thought, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that these activities should be banned, given that even a minor error can lead directly to the death of a participant, as can be seen in skydiving. However, a prohibition is impossible to enforce: many of these sports take place in remote locations, say, mountain cliffs, where surveillance is minimal. In addition, it is unrealistic to expect a police officer to follow every individual. Consequently, a prohibition may exist only on paper and may even drive the practice underground, making it harder to ensure basic safety standards.

People should be permitted to do any sports, as long as they understand risks and receive sufficient training. For example, those interested in deep ocean diving can join reputable clubs that offer participants appropriate equipment and qualified supervision; the training can make participation safer. This can be seen in the way new participants are accompanied by an expert who can teach them what to do when accidents occur, giving them the ability to recognise dangers and respond appropriately. Even with proper training and necessary precautions, no activity is entirely risk-free.

In conclusion, banning is neither practical nor effective. I am strongly convinced that allowing people freedom to choose under strict conditions of training and awareness is a more realistic approach.

paragraphs.text: The bar chart compares the amount of carbon emitted from oil, coal and gas in the UK between 1990 and 2010. The figures are given in millions of tons for five-year intervals.

Overall, gas emissions increased throughout the period, while emissions from coal and oil fell from their initial levels. Gas overtook the other two fuels by 2000 and remained the largest source in the final three surveyed years. Coal, by contrast, ended with the lowest figure.

In 1990, gas accounted for about 220 million tons of carbon emissions, the smallest amount among the three fuels. Its figure climbed to roughly 270 million in 1995 and 300 million in 2000, before reaching about 320 million in 2010. Coal began at approximately 310 million tons, the highest figure in 1990, but fell steadily to around 250 million in 2000 and then to 190 million tons in 2010.

Oil followed a less consistent downward pattern. Its emissions were about 270 million tons in 1990, then decreased to roughly 240 million in 1995. They recovered by around 20 million tons over the next five years, reaching about 260 million in 2000. After that, the figure fell again and finished at approximately 210 million tons in 2010. This was a net decrease of about 60 million tons, compared with a much larger fall of around 120 million tons for coal.

WRITING TASK 2
You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people think that, in today’s world, subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.

paragraphs: It is argued that what more important school subject between history and science-related and technology disciplines. Personally, I strongly believe that both kinds of subjects have their own advantages in different aspects and what kind of subjects depends largely on each country's situation.

On the one hand, for some developed countries where science and technology are already strong, over-emphasizing science-related subjects is unnecessary. Given that in those conditions, there is a national problem that is loss of cultural identity, history gives student knowledge which help them to understand others cultural and more likely to prioritize preservation of their own heritage. Added to this is the fact that history also guide people to develop a balanced country by learning through pre-societies, leading to a long-term advancement. This can seen in the way developed countries emphasize in history.

On the other hand, for less technological advance, prioritizing science-related subject is much more beneficial. Since technology and science is the key factor that drive drive overall national development, governments should give more support to this kind of subjects. This leads to building more labours at school and there are various scientific and technological project that foster students' interest about this field. This also means help create more scientists in key fields including: healthcare, agriculture, manufacturing, hence contributing to national growing. However, History is an important part, the subject without caring about the subjects, causing to an unbalanced society.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that history and science-related subjects is both important, they bring the merits in different aspects and how what subject is more important depend strongly on each country's specific background.

paragraphs.text: People debate whether history or science and technology should receive greater priority at school. In my view, both areas have distinct benefits, but the amount of attention given to each may depend on a country's needs. A school system should therefore consider its social and economic circumstances rather than apply the same priority everywhere.

On the one hand, history can be particularly valuable in a country where students are at risk of losing touch with their cultural heritage. Learning about earlier generations helps them understand how their communities developed and why certain traditions matter. For example, a class could examine local records and compare past customs with those still practised today. This gives students a concrete reason to preserve aspects of their heritage while also helping them understand other cultures. Even in a country with strong scientific education, such knowledge can add a social dimension that technical subjects alone may not provide.

On the other hand, a country with less advanced technology may have a stronger reason to invest in science-related subjects. If schools provide laboratories and practical projects, students can learn to test ideas, work with data and solve unfamiliar problems. Those skills could prepare some of them for further study and careers in healthcare, agriculture or manufacturing. More trained people in these areas may, in turn, contribute to national development. This is a possible chain of benefits rather than an automatic result of adding a subject to the timetable. Nevertheless, prioritising science should not mean removing history, since students also need to understand the society in which they will apply their skills.

In conclusion, history and science-related subjects both have important roles. History develops cultural understanding, while science and technology can strengthen practical skills. Their relative priority should depend on each country's particular needs, but students should still have the opportunity to study both.
